title: Debre Damo: Ethiopia's Sacred Monastery on a Plateau
excerpt: Perched on a flat‑topped mountain, this 6th‑century monastery is accessible only by rope – a true pilgrimage experience.
content:
Just 45 km from Adigrat, Debre Damo is one of Ethiopia's oldest and most revered monasteries. Founded in the 6th century by Abuna Aregawi, it sits atop a 3,000‑meter plateau with sheer cliffs on all sides. The only way up is by climbing a 15‑meter rope – an experience that has remained unchanged for centuries.

While the monastery itself is open only to men, the surrounding landscape and the journey are awe‑inspiring for all visitors. Our hotel can help you arrange transportation and a guide to this sacred site. The views from the base are spectacular, and the sense of history is palpable.

We recommend visiting early in the morning to avoid the heat. After descending, enjoy a packed lunch from our kitchen while overlooking the stunning scenery.
author: Canaan Hotel Team
